notes: Open by separating production leadership from farmer value capture; this slide is about the gap between output scale and realized income. Point to water stress first, then explain why crop leadership alone no longer lifts incomes. Expect a question on where to focus; answer: district clusters where irrigation, yields and storage gaps overlap.
title: Gujarat’s farm economy combines national leadership in cotton, groundnut, castor and spices with water and post-harvest gaps that cap farmer value capture

sections.heading: Commercial scale
sections.body: Agriculture and allied sectors contributed **15.0%** to Gujarat’s GSDP in 2023-24 at current prices, while the state remained a national leader in market-oriented crops with **8.6M tonnes** of cotton, **3.3M tonnes** of groundnut and **0.9M tonnes** of castor seed output in 2023-24.

sections.heading: Diversified crop basket
sections.body: Gujarat’s crop mix extends beyond staples into higher-value segments: cumin production reached **0.9M tonnes** and onion **2.0M tonnes** in 2023-24, while horticulture area stood at **2.0M hectares** in 2022-23. This diversification underpins stronger market linkage but raises dependence on storage, grading and price realization.

sections.heading: Water constraint
sections.body: The state’s gross cropped area was **10.5M hectares** in 2023-24, against net irrigated area of **4.8M hectares** in 2022-23. Groundwater stress remains structural: **158** assessment units were over-exploited, critical or semi-critical in Gujarat in 2023, limiting headroom for further income growth through input intensification alone.

sections.heading: Uneven productivity
sections.body: Gujarat leads on crop presence, not uniformly on yield. Cotton yield was **697 kg/ha** in 2023-24, while groundnut yield was **1,894 kg/ha** and onion **20.7 tonnes/ha**. The policy task is now district-specific yield improvement, especially where irrigation access, seed quality and agronomy execution diverge sharply.

sections.heading: Post-harvest bottleneck
sections.body: Market depth still lags production ambition. Gujarat had **226** APMCs and **8,070** regulated market yards/sub-yards in 2023-24, but cold storage capacity was **3.8M MT** in 2023 and warehousing remains uneven across crop belts. Farmers therefore produce at scale yet do not capture equivalent value across perishables and export-linked crops.

footnote: Source: Government of Gujarat Budget at a Glance 2024-25; Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Gujarat; Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare; Central Ground Water Board 2023; National Horticulture Board 2023 [[src:official]]
